papers.title: An improved statistical treatment for radioassay-based background projection incorporating part-to-part variation
papers.abstract: For low background experiments, prediction of the background from radioactivity in detector components is of critical importance. Radioassays are often conducted on small samples or individual parts, which may be subject to differences in production or handling resulting in a part-to-part variation. This part-to-part variation can have an impact on the total activity and is not presently captured by the averaging methods used to evaluate radioassays. We propose a new method for the averaging of radioassays to incorporate this part-to-part variation into predictions of the total activity of parts. We also consider how to add component activities based on assays for component groups that are simulated as a single entity.

papers.title: Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework
papers.abstract: We improve the Langevin model to incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative interactions between heavy quarks and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The transport coefficient of heavy quarks is evaluated by a potential scattering model in which both the short-range Yukawa interaction and the long-range string interaction are included. The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, $\Xi_c^0$, and $\Omega_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.

papers.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
papers.abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

papers.title: Unraveling QCD dynamics via charm-tagged jets with ALICE at the LHC
authors: Emma Yeats (on behalf of the ALICE Collaboration)
papers.abstract: The study of jet substructure provides tests of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and offers differential ways to study hadronization mechanisms. QCD predicts that jet radiation patterns depend on the mass and color charge of the initiating parton. Parton showers are sensitive to the different Casimir factors of quarks and gluons, and to the parton mass through the dead-cone effect. In this talk, we present three sets of $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jet measurements. First, we present the first measurement of the Energy-Energy Correlator (EEC) for $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jets. This observable reveals the detailed structure of QCD radiation from heavy quarks, allowing for a distinction between perturbative and non-perturbative effects in charm-quark showers. We then discuss measurements of the angular differences between three different axis definitions inside the jets. The three definitions offer different sensitivity to wide-angle soft radiation and systematically probe the radiation pattern from charm quarks. The final measurement regards jet angularities, which characterize the weighted angular distribution of the jet constituents. These powerful observables probe the parton shower, with sensitivity to parton-mass and Casimir-factor related effects that can be tuned by adjusting the importance of wide-angle radiation.

papers.title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays using effective field theory
papers.abstract: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.

papers.title: Ab initio calculations of ${\bar\delta_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
papers.abstract: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $\beta$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

papers.title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\text{NN}}}$ = 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
papers.abstract: Higher-order cumulants ($C_n$) of the event-by-event net-proton number ($\Delta N_{\mathrm{p}} = N_{\mathrm{p}} - N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}$) distributions are sensitive observables in the search for the QCD critical point. A reliable quantitative baseline for non-critical effects is essential for interpreting these observables. We calculate $C_2/\langle N_{\mathrm{p}} + N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}\rangle$, $C_3/C_1$, and $C_4/C_2$ in Au+Au collisions at collision energies $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.7$-$27$ GeV with the SMASH hadronic transport model. The collision-centrality, rapidity-window, and collision-energy dependences are reported. The cumulant ratios are predicted below the independent-Poisson baseline, with the suppression increasing toward more central collisions and larger rapidity windows. In 70-80% collisions, SMASH calculations lie above the STAR measurements for all three ratios, whereas in 0-5% collisions, the STAR $C_4/C_2$ value at 19.6 GeV lies below the SMASH reference with a pull of approximately $-2.7$. These results provide an independent non-critical hadronic baseline for assessing the model dependence of the observed data-model discrepancies.

papers.title: Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
papers.abstract: Identical charged pion femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions. At high baryon density, the differences between $\pi^+\pi^+$ and $\pi^-\pi^-$ Hanbury Brown--Twiss (HBT) radii may originate from both the third-body Coulomb effect and the initial-state isospin asymmetry. Since the latter is related to the equation of state (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, separating these two effects is essential. In these proceedings, we present the measurements of identical charged pion correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=3.0$, 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, 4.5, and 7.7 GeV collected by the STAR experiment. A correction procedure is developed to remove the residual third-body Coulomb effect. After correction, the extracted HBT radii of $\pi^+\pi^+$ and $\pi^-\pi^-$ become consistent within uncertainties. The results indicate that the observed charge dependence is dominated by the third-body Coulomb effect, while any remaining contribution from the initial-state isospin asymmetry to the relative HBT radius difference, $(R_{\pi^-}-R_{\pi^+})/R_{\pi^+}$, is constrained to be less than 5\% at the 95\% confidence level.

papers.title: Observation of Strong Directed Flow for $\phi$ Mesons in the High Baryon Density Region at RHIC
papers.abstract: We report measurements of the rapidity-odd directed flow ($v_{1}$) of $\phi$ mesons in 10--40\% Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{sNN}=3.0$--4.5 GeV from the STAR fixed-target program at RHIC, together with the collider-energy measurement at $\sqrt{sNN}=7.7$ GeV. Despite its mesonic nature, the $\phi$-meson $v_{1}$ exhibits a magnitude comparable to that of protons and $\Lambda$ baryons and is significantly larger than that of $K^{0}_{S}$ mesons in the high-baryon-density region. Comparisons with UrQMD calculations indicate that the observed $\phi$-meson directed flow is consistent with production through high-mass baryon resonances and the collective motion of baryons influenced by baryonic mean-field interactions. These results provide new experimental constraints on baryon-resonance production and strange-hadron transport dynamics in dense QCD matter.

papers.title: Recent Advances and Precision Measurements with the JYFLTRAP Double Penning Trap Mass Spectrometer
papers.abstract: High-precision atomic-mass measurements with the JYFLTRAP double Penning-trap mass spectrometer at the IGISOL facility provide direct information on decay energies, nuclear binding and shell evolution, isomer excitation energies, and masses relevant to nuclear astrophysics. Recent work has combined the phase-imaging ion-cyclotron-resonance (PI-ICR) method with established ion-purification and selective ion-production techniques to study low-yield nuclei and resolve isomeric states. At JYFLTRAP/IGISOL, mass-selective buffer-gas cooling, Ramsey cleaning, resonance ionization spectroscopy (RIS), phase-dependent cleaning, and species-resolved PI-ICR analysis are used in complementary combinations according to the ion yield and the required separation. Laser-frequency tagging correlates individual ion events with the corresponding laser frequency and enables state-resolved resonance-ionization spectra. Selected ion bunches are used for direct mass measurements with PI-ICR or time-of-flight ion-cyclotron resonance (TOF-ICR), for ion counting, or for post-trap decay spectroscopy. When multiple species or states are present, resolved PI-ICR phase spots allow the mass-measurement data to be assigned to the corresponding component. Examples from the recent program include high-precision $Q$-value measurements, neutron-deficient nuclei below $^{100}$Sn, neutron-rich fission fragments, rapid structural evolution around $N\approx60$, and rare-earth nuclei relevant to the astrophysical $r$ process.

papers.title: Design of nSPIRAL: a Neutron Spectrometric Position-Weighted Radial Array Long-Counter
papers.abstract: We present here the design of a neutron long counter intended to measure neutrons originating from radioactive decays or nuclear reactions. Like other similar detectors, it relies on a moderator (polyethylene) and $^{3}$He tubes. A novel feature of our design is the use of the weighting technique to achieve an efficiency that is virtually independent of the energy spectrum of the neutrons being measured; a property known as \textit{flat efficiency}. This approach offers two primary advantages: it yields a flatter efficiency response than conventional analysis methods, and it provides greater flexibility regarding the geometry of the long counter. The latter has enabled us to design the detector with almost every $^{3}$He tube positioned at a different distance from the neutron source, which allows us to perform not only neutron counting but also neutron spectroscopy.

papers.title: A Differentiable Surrogate for Loss-Dominated Ion Beam Transport
papers.abstract: Radioactive nuclei with extreme proton-to-neutron ratios provide unique probes of nuclear structure, fundamental symmetries, astrophysical processes, and applications such as medicine. However, their short half-lives and low production rates mean that experiments must work with few desired ions, often amid contaminant backgrounds exceeding the signal by six orders of magnitude. Efficiently isolating, transporting, and delivering these ions through multi-stage apparatus is therefore a central challenge. We introduce a differentiable probabilistic surrogate for ion-beam transport in regimes dominated by particle loss. The model jointly captures the survival probability of ions along the beamline and the evolving phase-space distribution of the surviving particles by combining discrete-time survival analysis with conditional normalizing flows. Applied to a high-dimensional electrostatic beamline, the resulting likelihood enables gradient-based optimization of operating voltages and inference of beam properties from sparse detector observations. Once trained, the surrogate provides millisecond-scale differentiable predictions, transforming particle-tracking simulations with hard losses into an inference-ready model for experimental design, beamline optimization, and future digital twins of experiments with rare nuclei.

papers.title: Axial-Vector Lattice Benchmarks Reveal a Common Medium Response of Meson Screening in Hot QCD
papers.abstract: Meson screening masses trace the evolution of hadronic correlations toward quasi-free quark--antiquark screening in hot QCD. Combining lattice QCD (LQCD) benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson--Schwinger baseline, we identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset, $x^\ast_{fg}=T^\ast_{fg}/T_c$: an operational matching scale based on the proximity of the axial-vector screening mass to its free-field reference, where $T_c$ is the pseudocritical temperature. On the finite interval $1\le T/T_c\lesssim x^\ast_{fg}$, independent light/strange and charm-containing lattice benchmarks are organized by a common medium-response function with one flavor-sector parameter. One axial-vector point fixes this parameter; the remaining axial-vector data test the temperature dependence of the response, and vector screening masses validate it without vector input. A reduced-mass interpolation then yields lattice-testable predictions for quasi-free onset scales and vector and axial-vector screening spectra in light--charm and open-bottom sectors.

papers.title: Unbiased Data-Driven Determination of the Nuclear Dipole Amplitude in the Color Glass Condensate
papers.abstract: Gluon saturation limits the growth of parton densities at small Bjorken-$x$ and is expected to be most pronounced in heavy nuclei. Yet quantitative extractions of the nuclear gluon dipole amplitude have long relied on parametrized initial conditions, introducing uncontrolled model dependence that obscures genuine nuclear effects. We introduce a physics-informed neural-network framework that embeds the collinearly improved Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution equation directly into the training objective, allowing the impact-parameter-averaged dipole amplitude to be determined from data without assuming a functional form for its initial condition. Applying this framework to forward-hadron nuclear-modification-factor and coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction data, we extract the $^{208}$Pb dipole amplitude at $x_0=0.01$ with QCD evolution and momentum-space positivity enforced throughout training. The evolved amplitude reproduces the measured cross sections across the available kinematic range and yields a saturation-scale ratio $Q_{s0,\mathrm{Pb}}^2/Q_{s0,p}^2 = 3.17^{+0.17}_{-0.10}$, consistent with simple geometric scaling. The extracted Pb initial condition is well described by a McLerran-Venugopalan-type form, in contrast to the proton, reflecting the higher color-charge density of a large nucleus. Using the same amplitude, we predict the rapidity dependence of the transverse-momentum ratio in $pp$, $p$Pb, and Pb$p$ collisions, finding agreement with recent LHCb measurements at low multiplicity without any system-dependent parameters. This work provides the first unbiased, data-driven determination of nuclear structure in the saturation regime and establishes a general strategy for embedding nonlinear evolution equations into machine-learning extractions of dynamically constrained observables.

papers.title: Hyper-Nuclei $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ Production in $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}}$ = 3 GeV Au+Au collisions at RHIC
papers.abstract: The STAR experiment reports the first measurement of the $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ hyper-nuclei yield as a function of rapidity and transverse momentum in 0-50% central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} =$ 3 GeV. The $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ is reconstructed through its three-body decay channel, $^4_{\Lambda}\rm{He} \rightarrow {}^{3}\rm{He} + \rm{p} + \pi^-$, with a statistical significance of about 9.5 standard deviations. We find that the yield of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ as a function of rapidity is consistent with that of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{H}$, and the rapidity-dependent yield ratio of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$/$^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{H}$ is consistent with that of $^3$He/t. All the measurements, as well as the transverse-momentum spectra, can be reasonably described by the JAM with a coalescence afterburner, suggesting a coalescence-based formation scenario for hyper-nuclei at this energy. The canonical thermal model reproduces the observed yield ratios but overpredicts the absolute hyper-nuclei yields.

papers.title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
papers.abstract: The radioisotope $^{229}$Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous $\gamma$-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of $\Delta E = (60\pm 50)~\mathrm{eV}$, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish $^{229}$Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.
